sections.title: Diagnosis Summary
sections.content:
**Primary Risk: The "Communication & Confidence Risk" Supply Chain Professional.**

Sneha, your profile presents a strong foundation. On paper, you are a credible Supply Chain and Inventory professional with a Resume & Experience Clarity score of 3.8, backed by measurable outcomes: driving inventory accuracy from 85% to 99% at SuperValu, eliminating an estimated €140k in annual carrying cost risk, and managing 500+ SKUs at Nestlé. Your Technical Readiness (3.7) and Answer Structure (3.6) show you understand the work. However, your Role-Specific Technical score of 3.2 and Behavioural Story score of 3.0 reveal a **Communication & Confidence Gap**.

**The Mapping Rule Analysis:**

While you clearly describe *what* you did (e.g., "Reduced order-picking errors by 20%", "Set reorder points based on historical consumption"), you may struggle when an interviewer pushes into the *how* and *why*: forecasting methodology, reorder point calculations, ERP/WMS reconciliation logic, or the stakeholder conversations behind procurement decisions. Under pressure, you risk sounding like someone who executed supply chain tasks rather than someone who owns the analytical reasoning and can defend trade-offs with confidence.

This "Competent Operator Who Can't Command the Room" persona is your primary hurdle. You look like a strong FMCG inventory candidate on the page, but in a Dublin hiring process you may under-sell your Nestlé and SuperValu depth when probed on S&OP, demand forecasting, or cross-functional influence.

sections.title: How This Risk Shows Up in Interviews
sections.content:
**Scenario A: The Resume Walkthrough (15–20m)**

**The Red Flag:** "Sneha, walk me through how you achieved 99%+ inventory accuracy at SuperValu across ERP and WMS. What was your baseline, how did you measure it, and what corrective actions did you take when discrepancies appeared?"

**Justification:** With Answer Structure at 3.6 and Communication & Confidence as your primary risk, you may deliver the headline (99% accuracy) but hesitate when asked for the measurement framework, cycle count frequency, or a specific discrepancy investigation. Interviewers in Ireland FMCG roles will probe until they hear operational proof—not just the outcome.

---

**Scenario B: The Technical Deep-Dive (30–45m)**

**The Red Flag:** "How do you set and review reorder points for 200+ SKUs? Walk me through the formula, data sources, and how you coordinate with procurement when lead times shift."

**Justification:** Your Role-Specific Technical score of 3.2 suggests you know the concepts but may default to "I used historical consumption and sales data" without articulating safety stock logic, ABC classification, seasonality adjustments, or how you validated that reorder points prevented stockouts without overstocking.

---

**Scenario C: The Behavioural & Influence Probe (15–20m)**

**The Red Flag:** "At Nestlé, tell me about a time you escalated a supply risk to protect production continuity. What was the risk, who did you influence, and what was the measurable result?"

**Justification:** Despite strong resume bullets on supplier scorecards and RFQ management, your Behavioural Story score of 3.0 means the "conflict", "escalation", and "stakeholder dynamic" may get buried under process description. Irish interviewers want to hear calm, confident ownership—not a checklist of tasks.

sections.title: Priority Fix Order

steps.title: The "Confidence + Structure" Drill
steps.content: Convert every SuperValu and Nestlé bullet into a 60-second STAR pitch. Record yourself aloud—focus on speaking numbers (85%→99%, 20% error reduction, 500+ SKUs) without rushing or trailing off. **Score Target:** Answer Structure 3.6 → 4.2, Behavioural Story 3.0 → 3.8

steps.title: Supply Chain "First Principles"
steps.content: Deep-dive into reorder point logic, demand forecasting inputs, safety stock, ABC analysis, and ERP/WMS reconciliation. Be able to explain *how* you measured inventory accuracy and order-picking errors—not just that you improved them. **Score Target:** Role-Specific Technical 3.2 → 4.0

steps.title: Tool-to-Value Mapping
steps.content: Practice explaining how SAP ERP, WMS, Power BI, and Excel specifically solved a business problem at SuperValu or Nestlé. Link Lean Six Sigma Green Belt to one concrete root-cause analysis you led. **Score Target:** Technical Readiness 3.7 → 4.5

steps.title: The Pressure Test
steps.content: High-speed mock interviews focused on follow-up probes: "What was your baseline?" "How did you validate that?" "What would you do differently?" Build confidence to hold your ground when interrupted. **Score Target:** Overall Average → 4.5

sections.content: Complete each phase before moving to the next. Do not skip ahead.

sections.title: Resume-Anchored Technical Prep
sections.content:
**Experience 1: SuperValu — 99%+ Inventory Accuracy (ERP & WMS)**

**Interviewer Probe:** "What was your accuracy baseline before 99%? How often did you run cycle counts? What were the top three root causes of discrepancies between ERP and WMS, and how did you fix them?"

**Likely Struggle:** Mapping to Role-Specific Technical (3.2), you may cite "daily and periodic stock counts" without defining accuracy formula (e.g., (1 − |system − physical| / total SKUs) × 100), discrepancy thresholds, or a specific investigation you led.

**Prep Drill:** Document: (1) baseline ~85% and measurement period, (2) count frequency and SKU sampling method, (3) top discrepancy types (receiving errors, picking variances, timing lags), (4) one corrective action with before/after. Practice: "We measured accuracy weekly across [X] SKUs; the main gap was [cause]; I implemented [action], moving accuracy from 85% to 99% over [timeframe], reducing carrying cost risk by an estimated €140k annually."

---

**Experience 2: SuperValu — 20% Order-Picking Error Reduction**

**Interviewer Probe:** "How did you diagnose the process gaps? What data did you analyse, what workflow did you redesign, and how did you prove the 20% improvement?"

**Likely Struggle:** You may describe "redesigning materials-availability workflows" without naming the KPI (pick accuracy rate, mis-pick count per 1,000 picks), the analysis method, or the control before/after.

**Prep Drill:** Prepare: (1) error definition and baseline rate, (2) data source (WMS logs, exception reports), (3) root cause (e.g., bin location ambiguity, batch sequencing), (4) process change, (5) validation period. Practice one 90-second walkthrough with a specific example.

---

**Experience 3: SuperValu — 200+ SKUs Reorder Point Management**

**Interviewer Probe:** "Walk me through how you set reorder points. What inputs—lead time, demand variability, service level—and how do you adjust when sales spike or a supplier is late?"

**Likely Struggle:** Defaulting to "historical consumption and sales data" without safety stock logic, coordination with procurement on PO timing, or how you prevented stockouts on high-velocity items.

**Prep Drill:** Pick 3 SKUs (A/B/C class). For each: average daily demand, lead time, safety stock assumption, reorder point formula, and one time you changed a reorder point after a trend shift.

---

**Experience 4: Nestlé — 500+ SKUs, Supplier Scorecards & RFQs**

**Interviewer Probe:** "What KPIs were on your supplier scorecards? Give me an example where you escalated a supply risk. How did you evaluate RFQ responses across cost, quality, and delivery?"

**Likely Struggle:** Listing "on-time delivery and quality KPIs" without weights, escalation criteria, or a specific RFQ decision you influenced.

**Prep Drill:** Document scorecard metrics (OTD %, quality reject rate, lead time variance). Prepare one escalation story: risk identified → data used → who you informed → outcome for production continuity. For RFQs: evaluation matrix and one sourcing decision.

---

**Project: MSc Thesis — Digital Procurement in Ireland (r = 0.651)**

**Interviewer Probe:** "What was your research methodology? How did you validate the correlation between digital procurement adoption and supply chain innovation? What practical recommendation would you give a food SME in Ireland?"

**Likely Struggle:** Academic framing without connecting to your operational experience—interviewers may see this as theoretical unless you bridge it to SuperValu/Nestlé context.

**Prep Drill:** Be ready to explain: sample (100 professionals), survey design, correlation interpretation (not causation), top barriers (cost, change resistance, digital literacy), and one actionable recommendation you'd implement in a retail FMCG setting.

sections.title: Interview Answer Construction Guidance
sections.content:
**Project:** Achieving 99%+ inventory accuracy at SuperValu.

**Baseline Answer (Score ~3.2 — Confidence & Depth Weakness):**
"At SuperValu I work as an Inventory Analyst. I use ERP and WMS systems to monitor stock. I do stock counts and investigate discrepancies. We improved accuracy to 99% and it helped with inventory optimisation and cost efficiency. I also work with procurement on reorder points."

**Fixed Answer (Score 4.5+ — Structured, Confident & Technical):**
"At SuperValu, inventory accuracy across ERP and WMS had been around 85%, which created carrying cost risk and unreliable replenishment signals for 200+ SKUs. (Situation) My task was to improve accuracy while keeping daily operations running across a high-volume retail environment. (Task) I established a weekly accuracy metric comparing system on-hand to physical counts, categorised discrepancies by root cause—receiving timing, pick variances, and master data errors—and redesigned our investigation workflow so every variance above [threshold] triggered a same-day corrective action with procurement looped in when PO timing was affected. (Action) Over [timeframe], accuracy moved from 85% to 99%+, order-picking errors dropped 20% through parallel workflow fixes, and we estimated €140k in annual carrying cost risk eliminated through tighter stock control. (Result)"

**Justification:** The "Fixed" version addresses Communication & Confidence by delivering a calm, complete STAR flow with specific metrics and methodology. It boosts Role-Specific Technical credibility by naming measurement logic, root causes, and cross-functional coordination—not just the headline number.

sections.title: High-Risk Questions (The Landmines)
sections.content:
"Walk me through how you measured inventory accuracy at SuperValu. What was the formula, baseline, and frequency of counts?" **(Risk: Role-Specific Technical 3.2)**

"How do you calculate reorder points for your 200+ SKUs? What safety stock assumptions do you use?" **(Risk: Role-Specific Technical 3.2)**

"You reduced order-picking errors by 20%—what was the baseline error rate, what data did you analyse, and what exactly did you change in the workflow?" **(Risk: Communication & Confidence)**

"At Nestlé, describe a supply risk you escalated. What triggered it, who did you influence, and what was the production impact?" **(Risk: Behavioural Story 3.0)**

"How do you evaluate supplier RFQ responses when cost, quality, and delivery conflict? Give me a real example." **(Risk: Role-Specific Technical 3.2)**

"Explain the correlation in your thesis (r = 0.651). What does it mean operationally for a food SME adopting e-procurement?" **(Risk: Technical depth vs. academic framing)**

"Tell me about a time you had to push back on procurement or a supervisor when stock levels were wrong. How did you communicate it?" **(Risk: Behavioural Story 3.0 + Confidence)**

"How would you run an S&OP-style review for a retail FMCG operation with high perishable turnover?" **(Risk: Role-Specific Technical 3.2)**

sections.title: Mock Interview Plan (Mentor-Led)

data.label: Session 1: Resume Walkthrough & Confidence Baseline
data.objective: Full resume flow under light interruption. Assess Answer Structure and confidence when speaking numbers aloud.

data.label: Session 2: Supply Chain Technical Deep-Dive
data.objective: Reorder points, forecasting, ERP/WMS accuracy, Nestlé supplier scorecards. Push on methodology until Role-Specific Technical improves.

data.label: Session 3: Behavioural & Cross-Functional Influence
data.objective: Escalation stories, procurement coordination, conflict with supervisors. Demand STAR with measurable outcomes.

data.label: Session 4: Final Pressure Test (Ireland FMCG Simulation)
data.objective: Rapid-fire technical + behavioural mix. Stockout scenario, supplier delay, accuracy crisis. Target 4.5+ across all areas.

sections.content:
**Session 1: Resume Walkthrough & Confidence Baseline**

**Focus:** SuperValu and Nestlé narrative flow; speaking metrics without rushing.

**Mentor Push:** Interrupt every 60 seconds with "What was the baseline?" and "How did you measure that?" Note hesitation, filler words, or trailing sentences—these signal Communication & Confidence gaps.

---

**Session 2: Supply Chain Technical Deep-Dive**

**Focus:** Reorder points, inventory accuracy measurement, demand forecasting, supplier scorecards, RFQ evaluation.

**Mentor Push:** Do not accept tool names (SAP, WMS) as answers. Demand formulas, data sources, and one concrete example per major resume bullet.

---

**Session 3: Behavioural & Cross-Functional Influence**

**Focus:** Supply risk escalation, procurement coordination, pushing back on stock decisions, cross-functional collaboration.

**Mentor Push:** If the story lacks conflict or a named stakeholder, stop and restart. Sneha must prove influence—not just task execution.

---

**Session 4: Final Pressure Test (Ireland FMCG Simulation)**

**Focus:** Scenario-based rapid fire: "A key SKU is stockout during peak weekend—walk me through your response"; "Supplier is 5 days late—what do you do?"; "Accuracy dropped to 92%—root cause and fix."

**Mentor Push:** Check if Role-Specific Technical and Behavioural Story have reached 4.5 target. Confidence under interruption is the pass/fail criterion.

sections.title: Expected Outcome
sections.content:
**Target Average Score: 4.5** (from a ~3.46 baseline on the composite diagnostic).

**Measurable Change Expected:**
- Move from "I improved accuracy to 99%" to "I measured accuracy weekly via [method], identified [root causes], and implemented [corrective actions]—moving from 85% to 99%+ and eliminating an estimated €140k carrying cost risk."
- Reorder point and forecasting answers include formulas, assumptions, and procurement coordination—not generic process description.
- Behavioural answers name stakeholders, conflict, and measurable outcomes with calm, confident delivery suited to Dublin FMCG hiring bars.

**After Persona:** A **Supply Chain & Inventory Analyst** who sounds operationally credible, analytically grounded, and confident under follow-up pressure—aligned with Ireland retail and FMCG interview expectations.

sections.title: How to Use This Plan

candidateSteps.title: Complete Week 1 Confidence + Structure Drill before Session 1
candidateSteps.content: Record yourself delivering STAR pitches for every SuperValu and Nestlé bullet. Listen for hesitation and filler words. This directly targets Answer Structure (3.6→4.2) and Behavioural Story (3.0→3.8).

candidateSteps.title: Build a one-page technical cheat sheet
candidateSteps.content: Document reorder point logic, accuracy formula, pick error KPI, and Nestlé scorecard metrics. Memorise numbers—85%→99%, 20% error reduction, 500+ SKUs, €140k carrying cost, r=0.651.

candidateSteps.title: Re-practice failed questions within 24 hours
candidateSteps.content: After each session, rewrite weak answers with baseline, method, and result. If you struggled with "How do you set reorder points?" in Session 2, prepare a full answer with one SKU example before Session 3.

candidateSteps.title: Do NOT proceed until previous session scores 4.5/5+
candidateSteps.content: Each session is a gate. If Session 1 confidence score is below 4.5/5, repeat Week 1 drills before Session 2. Rushing into technical depth without fixing delivery will not improve interview outcomes.

mentorSteps.title: Follow session instructions exactly
mentorSteps.content: Do not soften probes. Ireland FMCG interviews are operational and detail-oriented. If you skip "baseline" and "methodology" questions, you won't accurately assess score improvements.

mentorSteps.title: Probe until candidate breaks or admits knowledge boundary
mentorSteps.content: Find the limit on reorder logic, accuracy measurement, and escalation stories. Document "I don't know" moments—these define Week 2–3 prep focus.

mentorSteps.title: Provide written feedback on delivery, not just content
mentorSteps.content: Note confidence markers: pace, eye contact (if video), filler words, trailing off mid-answer. Content may be correct but delivery can still fail the Communication & Confidence bar.

mentorSteps.title: Reset expectations
mentorSteps.content: Passing Session 4 means interview-ready for supply chain/inventory roles—not a job guarantee. Use Session 4 as validation that Sneha can hold her ground under Irish FMCG-style follow-up questioning.

sections.content:
**Non-negotiable rule:**
If you fail Session 4 (score <4.5/5), repeat Sessions 2–4 in Week 5. Do not apply to roles until you pass Session 4.

**Timeline:**
- Week 1: Confidence + Structure Drill (STAR pitches, recorded practice)
- Week 2: Sessions 1–2 (Resume Walkthrough + Technical Deep-Dive)
- Week 3: Session 3 (Behavioural + Influence)
- Week 4: Session 4 (Final Pressure Test)
- Week 5: Buffer for repetition if needed

Start Week 1 today. Email your mentor when you've completed recorded STAR pitches for all SuperValu and Nestlé bullet points.
